event: A creak and thud sound occurs, and the task is to determine its location (left, right, or back) relative to a hypothetical robot standing by a fireplace and facing a wall-mounted TV.

sounding_object.description: The front door. It is a dark brown/black door, likely metal or heavy wood, featuring a large rectangular frosted glass panel with ornate black wrought iron scrollwork. It has a matching sidelight panel to its right (when viewed from inside the house). Approximate height of a standard door (around 2 meters) and width of about 0.9 meters.

reference_object.object_name: Fireplace with a black metal screen
reference_object.description: The hypothetical robot is standing by this object. The fireplace itself is not clearly and definitively visible in the video. A plausible location, based on typical living room layouts and items visible, would be on the wall to the right of the TV (from the initial camera's perspective, near the window and a white armchair) or on the wall opposite the TV. The robot's position is static.

facing_object.description: A large, black, flat-screen television, approximately 55-65 inches diagonally, mounted on the wall. It is positioned above a low, dark wooden entertainment console which has shelves containing various decorative items and electronics.

question: Imagine you are a robot standing by the fireplace with a black metal screen and facing the wall-mounted tv, when the creak and thud sound comes up, relative to where you are facing, where is the sounding object: left, right, or back? If the object is generally to your left and facing it requires turning less than 120 degrees left, choose 'left'. If the object is generally to your right and facing it requires turning less than 120 degrees right, choose 'right'. If the object is generally behind you and facing it requires turning 120 degrees or more, choose 'back'.
